subject: physics
title: Antiparticles, annihilation and pair production
key_idea: Every particle has an antiparticle with the same mass and opposite charge. A particle and its antiparticle annihilate, turning their mass into photons. A photon of enough energy can turn into a particle–antiparticle pair. Mass and energy are linked by ΔE = c²Δm.

blocks.text: For every type of particle there is a matching antiparticle. This section covers how the pair compare.

items: A particle and its antiparticle have the **same mass** and the same rest energy.
They have **opposite charge**: the positron is +1 and the antiproton is −1.
Neutral particles have neutral antiparticles. The antineutron is still a different particle from the neutron.
Other quantum numbers, such as baryon number and lepton number, are also opposite.
You can deduce the properties of an antiparticle from its particle, and the other way round.
An antiparticle has the same mass but opposite charge.
The positron is the antiparticle of the electron.

blocks.text: Mass and energy are equivalent. Particle physics uses units that suit the tiny values involved.

items.meaning: The energy gained by an electron accelerated through 1 V. 1 eV = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ J.
Units of energy. 1 MeV = 10⁶ eV and 1 GeV = 10⁹ eV.
Units of mass. A mass m has energy mc², so its mass in MeV/c² is its rest energy in MeV.
The energy equivalent of a particle's mass, mc².

items: 1 MeV/c² = 1.78 × 10⁻³⁰ kg.
The electron has a rest energy of 0.511 MeV, so its mass is 0.511 MeV/c².
The proton has a rest energy of about 938 MeV, so its mass is about 938 MeV/c².
ΔE = c²Δm links energy and mass.
A mass in MeV/c² is its rest energy in MeV.
Convert with 1 MeV = 1.60 × 10⁻¹³ J.

blocks.text: Electromagnetic radiation travels as photons, packets of energy. The energy of a photon depends on its frequency or wavelength.

items.meaning: A particle and its antiparticle meet and their mass becomes the energy of photons.
A photon of enough energy becomes a particle and its antiparticle.

items: An electron and a positron annihilate to give two photons: e⁻ + e⁺ → γ + γ.
Two photons are produced so that momentum is conserved. They travel in opposite directions.
Total energy is the rest energy of the pair plus their kinetic energy. For a pair at rest, each photon has 0.511 MeV.
A photon passes near a nucleus and becomes a pair: γ → e⁻ + e⁺.
The nucleus takes a little momentum, so momentum is conserved.
The photon needs at least twice the rest energy of one particle.
Any extra energy becomes the kinetic energy of the pair.

where: E(min) = least photon energy needed (J or MeV)
mc² = rest energy of one of the pair (J or MeV)

items: Annihilation turns a particle and antiparticle into photons.
Pair production needs a photon with at least 2mc² of energy.
Energy, momentum and charge are conserved in both.

checks.q: State two ways in which a proton and an antiproton are similar and one way in which they differ.
checks.a: They have the same mass and the same rest energy. They differ in charge: the proton is +1 and the antiproton is −1.

checks.q: An electron and a positron annihilate at rest. Explain why two photons are produced, and state the energy of each in MeV.
checks.a: The total momentum before is zero, so two photons travelling in opposite directions are needed to conserve momentum. Each has an energy of 0.511 MeV, the rest energy of one electron.

checks.q: Calculate the minimum photon energy, in MeV, needed to produce a proton and an antiproton. The rest energy of a proton is 938 MeV.

items: Know that the positron, antiproton, antineutron and antineutrino are the antiparticles of the electron, proton, neutron and neutrino.
Compare a particle and its antiparticle by mass, charge and rest energy in MeV.
Know the photon model of electromagnetic radiation, the Planck constant and E = hf = hc / λ.
Know annihilation and pair production and the energies involved.
Calculations do not need E = mc²: work in MeV and use the rest energies you are given.
Use ΔE = c²Δm for creation and annihilation. In annihilation, the mass lost appears as photon energy. In creation, the photon energy needed is at least the mass created × c².
Convert between MeV and GeV and between MeV/c² and GeV/c², and then to joules and kilograms.
1 GeV/c² = 1000 MeV/c², and 1 MeV/c² = 1.78 × 10⁻³⁰ kg.
Work in either set of units, but do not mix them.
